newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Taiwan details suspended South African deals.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan details suspended South African deals.

text.p: Taiwan released details on Monday of agreements with South Africa which were suspended after Pretoria's diplomatic switch from Taipei to Beijing.
The programmes and projects, totalling $842 million, included an offer of a $500 million deposit with South Africa's central Reserve Bank, Taiwan's Pretoria embassy said in a statement.

It said the Bank of Taiwan and International Commercial Bank of China had offered to deposit $500 million with the Reserve Bank "as balance of payments support" and the Bank had invited officials to visit South Africa to discuss the offer.
But Business Day newspaper quoted Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals as saying the money had not been accepted when it was offered a year ago.
"The loan was not needed, was refused and therefore never actually existed," the paper quoted Stals as saying.
Among the projects currently under negotiation are a $3.5 billion petrochemicals joint venture and the embassy said discussions would continue on the proposal.

Tuntex Distinct Corp and Kuangh-Hwa Investment Holding Co were involved from the Taiwanese side and South Africa's Central Energy Fund has been coordinating talks on behalf of a consortium including Sentrachem, Polifin, AECI Ltd, Sasol Ltd and Hoechst South Africa Ltd.

Taiwan is South Africa's seventh-largest trading partner with two-way trade totalling 5.7 billion rand ($1.24 billion) in 1995. Up to 43,000 jobs could be at risk if Taiwan disinvested entirely from South Africa, but this is seen as unlikely.

Pretoria was Taipei's biggest diplomatic ally. Its defection to mainland China -- which refuses ties to states recognising Taiwan -- leaves Taipei with diplomatic relations with just 29 minor nations.

The statement said programmes worth around $81 million had already been implemented and would not be affected by Foreign Minister John Chang's announcement last Thursday that his country would suspend projects pending restructuring of the ties between the two countries.
Another 25 million rand had already been provided for post-apartheid reconstruction and development projects and this money would not be withdrawn.

Among the other programmes suspended were a $30 million loan to state telecommunications utility Telkom for rural telephone systems. The deal had been negotiated but not yet signed, the statement said.

A loan agreement for $20 million signed with South Africa's MacSteel for steel exports to Taiwan had been suspended, as had a letter of intent signed for 56 G-5 model howitzers with an approximate value of $150 million, the statement said.
